_note: Two inputs of the ranking are judgements, not measurements. Each carries its reason so it can be challenged. Change a score or a weight, run make_report.py, and the ranking and every graph follow.

rust.reason: No null (Option), ownership rules out use-after-free and data races at compile time, matches must be exhaustive. What is left is logic bugs, explicit unwrap panics and release-mode integer overflow.

go.reason: Memory safe with a simple type system, but nil pointers and nil maps panic at run time, data races are possible (found by the -race tool, not the compiler), and an error value is easy to ignore.

csharp.reason: Memory safe; nullable reference types make the compiler warn about null, but they are warnings and the probe still found one unguarded null path that returned a 500. Data races are possible.

java.reason: Memory safe and very mature tooling, but null is everywhere (the probe crashed the handler on a null body until it was guarded) and data races are possible. Static analysers (NullAway, SpotBugs) narrow the gap but are extras.

node.reason: TypeScript types are erased at run time, so untrusted JSON is not protected by them; null and undefined both exist. One thread per process removes most data races, and the npm dependency tree is large.

python.reason: Dynamic typing means type and attribute mistakes show up only when that line runs. The project already offsets this with 1,700+ tests, an independent oracle, fuzzing and mutation testing; that is effort spent, not a property of the language.
All of the system exists in Python: the engine, 1,736 tests, the queue (Celery), the API (FastAPI), MongoDB access, the rule pack (YARA-X bindings). Nothing to rewrite.

node.reason: The team reads JavaScript from the console, and Mongo and queue libraries exist, but every module, test and the YARA-X integration would be rewritten.

go.reason: Quick to learn and to deploy, strong stdlib and queue/Mongo libraries; everything is still a rewrite, and the YARA-X bindings are not first-class.

csharp.reason: Excellent platform and tooling; a full rewrite, a new runtime to install on the on-premises server, and nobody on the team has shipped in it.

java.reason: Excellent ecosystem; a full rewrite, a heavier runtime and slower start, and nobody on the team has shipped in it.

rust.reason: YARA-X itself is written in Rust, so the rule engine could be used natively; but the steepest learning curve of the six, a full rewrite, and the weakest fit with a deadline measured in days.
